title: DATASET ON PREVALENCE, GENOTYPIC CHARACTERIZATION, AND RISK FACTORS OF SALMONELLA ENTERICA ALONG THE BROILER SLAUGHTER CONTINUUM IN PERI-URBAN KENYA
author: Angela Mwangi
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0
description: This dataset supports the findings of a cross-sectional study investigating Salmonella enterica contamination along the broiler slaughter continuum in smallholder farms in Kiambu and Nairobi Counties, Kenya. A total of 400 samples were collected from 100 farms across four sample types: pooled broiler carcasses, evisceration table swabs, carcass rinse water, and scalding water. The dataset contains two components. The first is sample metadata, which includes farm identifiers, county of origin (Kiambu or Nairobi), sample type, and collection point along the slaughter continuum. The second is microbiological isolation results, which include Salmonella enterica detection outcomes per sample following ISO 6579-1:2017 protocols, PCR confirmation status for the invA gene.
